newsitem.title: EGYPT: Lebanon defends ban on potato imports from Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon defends ban on potato imports from Egypt.

text.p: Egypt attacked on Sunday a Lebanese decision to ban imports of Egyptian potatoes and said countermeasures against Lebanon might be in order.
Lebanon defended its decision by saying it was not aimed at Egypt but to protect home-grown potatoes.

"This (the ban) will have undesirable effects on trade relations. Egypt would have preferred this step had not been taken, a step which necessarily calls for a look at measures to counter it," Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters.
"There are question-marks about this. The position the Lebanese government took on this is incomprehensible," he added.

Lebanese Agriculture Minister Shawki Fakhoury told Reuters: "This decision was taken in light of the national interest. It was not intended to anger Egypt. We have the right to protect local production and this is why we took the decision."
He said the ban, decided two weeks ago, included imported potatoes from Syria, Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
"When I realised that big quantities of imported potatoes are being stored just two weeks before local potatoes are put on the market, I had to impose the ban," Fakhoury added.

The Lebanese government, trying to cut the cost of the country's food imports, plans to keep out products that can be grown at home from October 1. Fakhoury said the ban on Egyptian potatoes was part of the same campaign.

Asked to comment on Moussa's remarks, Fakhoury said: "The issue must have been reported in a distorted way to our colleague Moussa. The decision has nothing to do with Lebanon's relations with Egypt. It is only an act of national protection for local production."
The Egyptian government is especially sensitive about its exports of potatoes, an important cash crop and a frequent irritant in trade relations with the European Union.
Last year France restricted imports of Egyptian potatoes because some of them had brown rot.
Moussa said he hoped Lebanese trade policy would take into account all aspects of Egyptian-Lebanese relations.

"Trade between the two countries is something that should be pushed forwards, not dragged backwards. Any problems can be solved through direct dialogue, not by decrees which lead to tension in commercial relations," he added.
Apples are one of Lebanon's main exports to Egypt.
